subject: Quiet window — quick recap and one question on fit/timing
messages:
From: Diego Fernández <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@seaforth.ai>, Alicia Mora <alicia.mora@seaforth.ai>
Date: 2028-05-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap & quick next-step ask

Hi Sam / Alicia,

Thanks again for taking time yesterday — appreciated the openness on where Seaforth is headed with inference for your ingestion pipelines. Quick recap and one ask so we can align internally: 

Recap (high level)
- Goal: reduce per-query inference cost by 40–60% while keeping 95th pct latency under 120ms for 512-token windows.
- Primary workloads: enrichment + reranking on nightly batches, some low-latency API for live scoring (spikes ~200 qps).
- Constraints: must support customer data routing to a private VPC and SOC2 evidence for controls.

Notes from our chat
- You currently use a mix of CPU-bound endpoints for batch and a third-party hosted low-latency model for live scoring.
- Your procurement window is June–July per Alicia.

Ask: quick fit signal
- Could you reply with one line on fit: "Good fit / Maybe / Not a fit" and (if possible) whether procurement stays on the June–July timeline? That will help me prioritize the right next step (pilot scope vs. smaller eval).

Attached: discovery-recap.pdf (one-page summary) and pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (estimate ranges we discussed).

Proposed next step (if good fit): 45-min technical pilot kickoff the week of May 20 to map throughput targets and infra.

If now isn't the right time, a short "not now" is totally fine — I won't follow up aggressively.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Diego Fernández
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
M: +1 415-555-0172

--
Attachments: discovery-recap.pdf (summary), pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (estimate)

From: Diego Fernández <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@seaforth.ai>, Alicia Mora <alicia.mora@seaforth.ai>
Date: 2028-05-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & quick next-step ask

Hi Sam / Alicia —

Just nudging this thread in case it got buried. Quick reminder of my one-line ask: could you share a short signal on fit (Good fit / Maybe / Not a fit) and confirm whether the June–July procurement window still holds? If helpful I can send a trimmed pilot proposal that only covers the live scoring slice (smaller scope).

If the timeline has shifted or you're blocking on internal budget/priortization, totally understood — a sentence is enough. If it helps to route this to someone else on your side, let me know and I can brief them directly.

Thanks,
Diego

From: Alicia Mora <alicia.mora@seaforth.ai>
To: Diego Fernández <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-09T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & quick next-step ask

Hi Diego — apologies for the delay. Short answer: Maybe.

Alicia's note to you: we thought the technical fit looks promising for the live scoring piece, but budget and an internal reprioritization mean procurement is likely to slip. We have an executive review next week and expect a decision on whether to fund any new infra pilots this quarter — probably not, but Q4 looks more realistic.

Request: could you do two small things for us?
1) Confirm whether you can keep the pricing-sheet ranges in your attached estimate valid through the end of Q3. If not, what would change materially?
2) Share a 1-page pilot options table that scopes a minimal live-scoring pilot (<=2 GPUs, 30 days) vs. a bigger pilot that includes nightly batch offload. One page is great — we want to present something concise in the exec review.

If you can send both by EOD Thursday I will push them into the packet for the review. If the answer is "not likely to get funded now," still useful to have those artifacts so we can reopen quickly in Q4.

Thanks — Sam is looped on this for budget context.

Best,
Alicia Mora
Head of Platform Engineering | Seaforth Analytics
